doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Second day: self-education, reading and libraries
summary: Berger opens the second day, August 7, 1992, and asks about Carter's informal education and reading.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: This is the second tape and the second day of our interviews with Benny Carter. It’s now August 7th, 1992, the eve of Benny’s eighty-fifth birthday. We left off with his first real big band around 1932, 1933, but before we pick up on that, I’d just like to digress on a couple of things that have occurred when I listened to things you said earlier that I didn’t follow up on. One was we went through the episode of how you left school involuntarily before finishing the eighth grade and never went back for formal education. But obviously there’s been a lot of informal education taking place, and just the fact that you’re so well read and seem to have spent large portions of your life just reading, not about music, about everything. I’m just wondering, did that start that early in life? Already when other people were going to elementary school, were you continuing to educate yourself informally?

Oh, I don’t know. You might say it like that. I was probably trying to make up for what I might have missed, or what I had surely missed, you know, in the way of formal education. But, gee, I don’t know whether . . . as I say, nothing I have done has actually been planned. It just . . . I’ve always just gone along with the flow, and somehow or other it has, I don’t . . . brought me to the other side of the river.
So you never set out and said, “Gee, I’m not going to school, I’m going to look at this in this kind of book,” but . . .
I don’t remember that I ever unconsciously, or consciously, rather, entertained those kinds of thoughts.
Do you remember going to libraries, though, just informally or [unclear]?
Oh yes, yes. Yes, that I did.
Yes, pretty much on my own, sure.
And what, would you just browse through things and pick out . . .
Yeah, and I would borrow books, you know, of course.
And I might add that I would return them. [laughter]
Well, if you still have any, the fines could be enormous at this point.
No, I have none that I borrowed.

Because I know in the past you’ve mentioned a couple of books that you remembered from your childhood, really, that you were interested in seeing again. I just was wondering how you came upon them in the first place, and I guess it was part of this process of you would just go to a library, browse around, and find something that struck you.
I guess so. I don’t even remember titles at the moment.
